$comment: Occupation taxonomy. O*NET-SOC codes as the backbone reference (approximate where a role is emerging and has no clean SOC). Synonyms are matched against cleaned posting titles (lowercased, seniority stripped). Seeded deepest for the launch vertical (architecture); every profession is accepted and mapped from day one. Log unmapped titles, review, extend.

occupations.title: Architect
occupations.desc: Designs buildings and the documents that get them built. Balances program, code, budget, and intent across years-long projects.

license.label: State architecture license (RA/ARB) — registration required to practice/title

occupations.title: Computational Designer
occupations.desc: Turns design intent into code. Writes algorithms and scripts to generate geometry, automate documentation, and solve problems that would be impossible by hand.

occupations.title: BIM Manager
occupations.desc: Owns the digital model across a project team. Sets standards, coordinates disciplines, and makes sure every drawing in the set comes from one source of truth.

occupations.title: Creative Technologist
occupations.desc: Sits between design and engineering. Builds prototypes and interactive experiences for brands, museums, and studios — making technical ideas physical and legible.

occupations.title: Data Analyst
occupations.desc: Turns messy business data into decisions. Runs the queries, builds the dashboards, and translates what patterns actually mean for the people making the calls.

occupations.title: UX Designer
occupations.desc: Designs how software should feel to use. Researches users, maps flows, sketches interfaces, and defends the human experience against every other project pressure.

occupations.title: Product Designer
occupations.desc: Owns a digital product's look, feel, and story end to end. Combines visual design, systems thinking, and close collaboration with engineers and PMs.

occupations.title: Interior Technologist
occupations.desc: Bridges architecture and interior design with the technical detail work. FF&E, materials, specification writing, and coordination with contractors.

occupations.title: Urban Planner
occupations.desc: Shapes cities and neighborhoods over years, not weeks. Works with public policy, GIS data, and community input to design zoning, mobility, and public space.

license.label: State landscape-architecture license in most states
Contractor licensing varies by state; certifications (CCM) common
Brokerage/contractor licenses depending on activity
Often requires PE/RA background
PE license required to sign/seal structural work
PE license required for responsible charge
PE license required for sign-off roles

occupations.title: Supply Chain Analyst
synonyms: planificador de la cadena de suministro

license.label: CPA license required for public accounting/attest work
FINRA licenses required for securities roles; CFA common
CPA typically required for external audit
Credentialing exams (SOA/CAS) effectively required
State insurance licenses for some lines
Licenses/certifications by sector (FINRA, AML)
Bar admission required — jurisdiction-specific
State RN license (NCLEX) required
State APRN license + national certification required
Certification (CMA/RMA) commonly expected; varies by state
DPT degree + state PT license (NPTE) required
PharmD + state pharmacist license (NAPLEX) required
RD/RDN credential + state licensure in most states
Certifications (ACRP/SoCRA) commonly expected
State clinical license (LPC/LMFT/LCSW) required
State license required for clinical roles (LCSW)
State psychologist license required
State teaching certification required for public schools
State administrator certification typically required
PE required for sign-off roles; not for most product/manufacturing roles
PE required for public-facing/utility sign-off; not for product roles
State/journeyman electrician license required
State/journeyman plumbing license required
State license + EPA 608 certification required
Code certifications (AWS) required for structural work
Food-safety certification (ServSafe) typically required
FAA certification via the airline required
FAA commercial/ATP certificate required
State real-estate license required

occupations.title: Architectural Drafter
occupations.desc: Turns an architect's design into the precise drawings a project gets built from. Lives in Revit and AutoCAD; owns the accuracy of the set.

occupations.title: Teaching Assistant
occupations.desc: Supports a classroom teacher and the students who need the most help. The most common way into the education profession.

license.label: Paraprofessional requirements vary by state

occupations.title: Building Surveyor
occupations.desc: Inspects buildings for defects, compliance, and condition. Advises on repair, regulation, and value across a building's life.

license.label: Licensure/registration varies by jurisdiction

occupations.title: Maintenance Technician
occupations.desc: Keeps equipment and buildings running. Diagnoses faults, makes repairs, and prevents the breakdowns before they happen.

occupations.title: Police Officer
occupations.desc: Enforces the law and responds to incidents in a community. Public-sector work with clear rank structure and pension.

license.label: Police academy + state certification (POST) required

occupations.title: AI Engineer
occupations.desc: Builds products on top of large language models and machine-learning systems — retrieval pipelines, agents, evaluation, and the engineering that makes AI reliable in production.

occupations.title: MLOps Engineer
occupations.desc: Owns the path from model to production: training pipelines, deployment, monitoring, drift, and the infrastructure that keeps machine learning running.

occupations.title: Prompt Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs, tests, and versions the instructions that steer large language models — prompt systems, evaluation suites, and guardrails for AI products.

occupations.title: Computer Vision Engineer
occupations.desc: Teaches machines to see: detection, segmentation, tracking, and imaging pipelines for products from robotics to medical imaging.

occupations.title: NLP Engineer
occupations.desc: Builds systems that read and write language — classification, extraction, search, and LLM-based applications over text.

occupations.title: Robotics Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs and programs robots — kinematics, control systems, perception, and the integration of hardware with autonomy software.

occupations.title: AI Product Manager
occupations.desc: Product management where the product is a model: scoping AI capabilities, evaluation criteria, data strategy, and shipping ML-powered features responsibly.

occupations.title: Data Architect
occupations.desc: Designs how an organization's data lives: warehouses, lakes, models, governance, and the pipelines between them.

occupations.title: Cook
occupations.desc: Prepares and plates food to order on a working line, under time and consistency pressure. Distinct from the chef who runs the kitchen.

occupations.title: Automotive Technician
occupations.desc: Diagnoses and repairs vehicles, from brakes and diagnostics to full engine work. Includes auto, diesel, and heavy-equipment technicians.

occupations.title: Physician

license.label: MD/DO, residency, and state medical license (7+ yrs of training)

occupations.desc: Diagnoses and treats illness across a specialty, from primary care to surgery. Long training and licensure gate the role.

occupations.title: Paramedic

license.label: State paramedic license (NREMT); 1–2 yr accredited program

occupations.desc: Delivers emergency medical care in the field and in transit, from ambulances to air rescue. Licensed, high-stakes, and shift-based. EMT is the tier below, not a synonym.

occupations.title: Dental Hygienist

license.label: State RDH license; accredited dental-hygiene associate degree (~3 yrs)

occupations.desc: Cleans teeth, takes radiographs, and screens for oral disease alongside a dentist. A licensed clinical profession, one tier above dental assisting.

occupations.title: Medical Scribe
occupations.desc: Documents a clinician's visits in real time so the clinician can focus on the patient. A common on-ramp into healthcare and medical school.

occupations.title: Developer Advocate
occupations.desc: The bridge between a technical product and the developers who use it: docs, demos, talks, and feedback carried back to engineering.

occupations.title: Penetration Tester
occupations.desc: Attacks systems on purpose, with permission, to find the holes before an adversary does. Offensive security, red-teaming, and reporting.

occupations.title: Growth Marketer
occupations.desc: Owns a growth number and runs experiments across acquisition, activation, and retention. Half marketer, half analyst.

occupations.title: Conversation Designer
occupations.desc: Designs how people talk to software: chatbots, voice assistants, and the scripts and flows behind conversational AI.

occupations.title: Data Annotator
occupations.desc: Labels and rates the data that trains and aligns machine-learning models, including the human feedback behind modern AI.

occupations.title: Genetic Counselor

license.label: Master's in genetic counseling + ABGC board certification; state licensure in most states

occupations.desc: Interprets genetic test results and guides patients through the risks and decisions that follow. Master's-level and licensed.

occupations.title: Human Factors Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs tools, interfaces, and workspaces around how people actually perceive and move. Ergonomics with engineering rigor.

occupations.title: Forensic Accountant
occupations.desc: Follows the money through fraud, disputes, and investigations. Accounting used as evidence rather than record-keeping.

occupations.title: Cartographer
occupations.desc: Turns spatial data into maps and models, from survey to screen. Overlaps GIS but centered on the map itself.

occupations.title: Sound Designer
occupations.desc: Builds the audio of games, film, and products: effects, foley, mixing, and the feel a scene gets from what you hear.

occupations.title: Wind Turbine Technician
occupations.desc: Installs and services wind turbines, often hundreds of feet up. One of the faster-growing skilled trades.

occupations.title: Solar Installer
occupations.desc: Mounts and wires photovoltaic systems on roofs and in fields. A green-economy trade with steady demand.

occupations.title: Drone Pilot
occupations.desc: Flies uncrewed aircraft for survey, inspection, film, and delivery. Commercial work requires a remote-pilot certificate.

occupations.title: Brewmaster
occupations.desc: Runs the recipe and the process behind beer and spirits at production scale, from grain to package. Includes brewers and distillers.

occupations.title: Perfusionist
occupations.desc: Runs the heart-lung machine that keeps a patient alive during cardiac surgery. A small field with high stakes and specialized training.

occupations.title: Patent Agent
occupations.desc: Drafts and prosecutes patents before the patent office. Technical enough to read the invention, credentialed without being a lawyer.

occupations.title: Sommelier
occupations.desc: Curates and serves wine and builds a beverage program in restaurants and hospitality. A certified craft of taste.

occupations.title: Robotics Technician
occupations.desc: Builds, calibrates, and maintains robots and automated lines on the floor. The hands-on complement to the robotics engineer.

occupations.title: Medical Sales Representative
occupations.desc: Sells prescription drugs, devices or diagnostics to clinicians and hospitals on an assigned territory.

occupations.title: Quality Inspector
occupations.desc: Checks parts, products, vehicles or cargo against a specification and signs off or rejects them.

occupations.title: Laboratory Technician
occupations.desc: Runs samples, instruments and tests in a laboratory and records the results.

occupations.title: Machinist
occupations.desc: Sets up and runs lathes, mills and CNC machines to cut metal parts to a drawing.

occupations.title: Construction Superintendent
occupations.desc: Runs the site day to day: crews, subcontractors, sequence, safety and the schedule.

occupations.title: Project Scheduler
occupations.desc: Builds and maintains the programme for a project: activities, logic, resources and the critical path.

occupations.title: Quantity Surveyor
occupations.desc: Prices, measures and controls the cost of construction work from tender to final account.

occupations.title: Engineering Manager
occupations.desc: Leads a team of engineers: hiring, priorities, delivery and the people work.

occupations.title: Program Manager
occupations.desc: Coordinates a set of related projects toward one outcome, across teams and over years.

occupations.title: Systems Engineer
occupations.desc: Owns how the parts of a complex product fit together: requirements, interfaces, integration and verification.

occupations.title: Controls Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs and programs the control systems that run machines and plants: PLCs, instrumentation, SCADA.

occupations.title: Manufacturing Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs how a product gets made: the process, the tooling, the line and its yield.

occupations.title: Test Engineer
occupations.desc: Plans and runs the tests that prove hardware does what its design says, and writes up what it did instead.

occupations.title: Electronics Technician
occupations.desc: Builds, tests and repairs electronic assemblies and instrumentation.

occupations.title: Hardware Engineer
occupations.desc: Designs boards, chips and RF front ends: schematics, layout, bring-up.

occupations.title: Health and Safety Officer
occupations.desc: Keeps people from getting hurt at work: risk assessments, inspections, incident investigation, compliance.

occupations.title: Security Guard
occupations.desc: Protects people, premises and goods on site: patrols, access control, screening, response.

occupations.title: Procurement Specialist
occupations.desc: Buys what the company needs: suppliers, tenders, contracts, prices and lead times.

occupations.title: Logistics Coordinator
occupations.desc: Moves goods on time: carriers, customs, shipping paperwork, dangerous goods, the warehouse handoff.

occupations.title: Chemist
occupations.desc: Analyses, formulates and characterises substances in a lab, and writes the method down.

occupations.title: Dental Assistant
occupations.desc: Works chairside with the dentist: instruments, suction, x-rays, sterilisation, the patient.

occupations.title: Dentist
occupations.desc: Diagnoses and treats teeth, gums and mouths, in general practice or a specialty.

license.label: Dental degree (DDS/DMD or equivalent) and a state or cantonal licence to practise

occupations.title: Veterinarian
occupations.desc: Diagnoses and treats animals, from companion pets to herds, and advises the people who keep them.

license.label: Veterinary degree (DVM or equivalent) and a state or cantonal licence to practise

occupations.title: Occupational Therapist
occupations.desc: Helps people do the everyday things an illness, injury or disability got in the way of.

license.label: Occupational therapy degree and state licence (NBCOT in the US)

occupations.title: EMT
occupations.desc: Responds to emergencies and gives basic life support on the way to hospital.

license.label: EMT certification (NREMT or state) at the basic or advanced level

occupations.title: Pharmacy Technician
occupations.desc: Prepares and dispenses medicines under a pharmacist, and keeps the stock and the records straight.

occupations.title: Nursing Assistant
occupations.desc: Gives hands-on daily care under a nurse: washing, moving, feeding, observing, being there.

occupations.title: Food Service Worker
occupations.desc: Keeps a kitchen or counter running: prep, plating, dishes, stock, the pace of service.

occupations.title: Waiter
occupations.desc: Takes the order, brings the food and drink, and reads the table.

occupations.title: Receptionist
occupations.desc: First face and voice of the place: welcomes, checks in, answers, routes, keeps the desk running.

occupations.title: Administrative Assistant
occupations.desc: Keeps an office or a team organised: calendars, documents, orders, the phone, the follow-ups.

occupations.title: Truck Driver
occupations.desc: Drives goods on the road, from parcels across town to loads across the country.

license.label: Commercial driving licence (CDL class A/B in the US, C/CE in Europe)

occupations.title: Field Service Technician
occupations.desc: Installs, services and repairs equipment where it is: customer sites, homes, plants, roads.

occupations.title: Project Engineer
occupations.desc: The engineer on a project who turns the design into a delivered thing: scope, submittals, vendors, the site.

occupations.title: General Manager
occupations.desc: Runs a site, branch, region or business unit end to end, with the P&L.

occupations.title: Production Supervisor
occupations.desc: Runs a shift or a line: people, output, quality, safety, the plan for tomorrow.

occupations.title: Payroll Specialist
occupations.desc: Gets everyone paid correctly and on time, and keeps the tax and social filings right.

occupations.title: ERP Consultant
occupations.desc: Configures and rolls out enterprise systems (SAP, Dynamics, Workday, Salesforce) for the people who have to use them.

occupations.title: Manufacturing Technician
occupations.desc: Builds the product on the floor: assembly, machines, process steps, the paperwork that proves it.

occupations.title: Environmental Scientist
occupations.desc: Measures and explains what a site, a project or a company does to air, water, soil and habitats.

occupations.title: Content Moderator
occupations.desc: Reviews what people post against the rules of the platform, and decides.

occupations.title: Merchandiser
occupations.desc: Makes the product show up and sell in store: displays, stock, promotions, the planogram.

occupations.title: Retail Sales Associate
occupations.desc: Serves customers on the shop floor: advice, the sale, the till, the shelves.

occupations.title: Business Development Manager
occupations.desc: Finds and opens the next accounts, partners and markets, before there is a pipeline to manage.

occupations.title: Housekeeper
occupations.desc: Keeps rooms, wards, offices and buildings clean and ready, to a standard and a clock.
